data_plan: 15-minute bars, universe = BTCUSDT / ETHUSDT / SOLUSDT (the SYMBOLS triple of Stratex/rigorous_backtest/rd/common.py, drawn from the crypto30 panel of rd2/panels.py), Binance Vision USDT-M futures monthly klines via the programme's verified loader (data_feed.load_dataset) — the identical panel and loader the Box Theory and S-RD1 declared runs used (months 2023-10..2026-10, 108,192 bars per symbol, zero missing bars; provenance = per-symbol csv_sha256 must equal ig/box_theory_provenance.json). Free and keyless; no new data source is introduced. The run must state the exact panel, source and date range it used and apply walk-forward folds W1..W5 per programme convention. The run is a separate, later step and is NOT part of the declaring PR.

declared_conventions.bar_resolution_limit: 15-minute OHLC bars cannot reveal the intra-bar path, queue position at a level, or partial fills. This declaration compensates with the frozen fill haircut (see fill_model) and discloses the residual optimism that remains: once a level is traded through by the margin, a unit is assumed filled IN FULL at the level price. A live book could still leave a partial. The haircut is biased conservative on the fill CONDITION (touch fills — the dominant fantasy component of naive grid simulators — are excluded entirely and counted in the run's stats) and is limit-order-faithful on fill PRICE (a real limit order fills at its limit or better). Even so, a PASS measures a haircut kline simulation, not a live book; it earns a forward-test candidate slot where real fills decide, nothing more.
declared_conventions.counting_rule: One completed round trip — one buy fill plus its matching exit fill (grid sell, teardown or end-of-data) — is ONE trade, attributed to folds by its ENTRY (buy fill) time, the programme's entry-time convention. Open units are always closed by teardown or at the end of the data, so every buy fill has exactly one matching exit fill and no open inventory enters the judgement. Per-fill counts are reported in the run's stats alongside the trade count; the bar's >= 200 counts ROUND TRIPS.
declared_conventions.degenerate_range: If the trailing window's P90 <= P10 (zero-width range), no grid is placed for that epoch: no lines, no fills, until the next placement. No substitute range is invented.
declared_conventions.fill_sequencing: Within any bar, exits are evaluated only for units open at that bar's START (a unit bought in bar i is managed from bar i+1 — the programme's no-same-bar-exit convention). A line whose unit sold in bar i cannot buy again in bar i (the intra-bar path is unknowable; re-buying after a sale in the same bar would assume the favourable ordering). Buys on different lines in the same bar are independent and all may fill (a cascading bar genuinely sweeps every resting level it trades through). Placement bars are processed in this order: fills under the old grid, teardown of open units at the placement bar's close, placement of the new grid from the trailing window ending at that bar.
declared_conventions.forward_sizing: NOT part of this family's backtest identity — the bar judges per-unit expectancy / profit factor, which are sizing-invariant (programme practice). IF the candidate ever reaches forward testing it inherits FWD-006 with this declared mapping: unit notional = 1% of venue equity; the per-symbol inventory cap (10 units) therefore caps inventory at 10% of equity notional, equal to FWD-006's MAX_POSITION_PCT (0.10); a full inventory suffering a 20% adverse gap loses 2% of equity, equal to the FWD-006 strategy heat cap (0.02). FWD-006's per-trade 0.1% risk rule does NOT map onto passive fills — a grid unit has no stop; the inventory cap plus the 24h teardown are this family's risk controls, and that mismatch is recorded here rather than papered over.
declared_conventions.inventory_carry: No inventory carries across epochs. At every re-placement (every 96 bars) all open units are force-closed at the placement bar's close with full costs (exit_reason TEARDOWN). A real grid bot could carry inventory into the next grid; flattening is the conservative choice (it pays full round-trip costs on every unit at most 24h after entry) and keeps every unit's target inside its birth grid. Adding carry would be a variant.
declared_conventions.long_only: The grid is LONG-ONLY (the classic spot-style grid construction, applied to the futures panel's prices): the sell side exists only as the paired exit of a previously bought unit. No short inventory is ever opened. A symmetric long/short grid is a different family and would need its own declaration.
declared_conventions.panel_scope: v1 tests BTCUSDT / ETHUSDT / SOLUSDT at 15m ONLY — the programme's own SYMBOLS triple, so rd.common.full_report / check_bar / holdout_check apply verbatim, and the three deepest Binance USDT-M books in crypto30 (tightest spreads, deepest queues). The haircut is thereby calibrated at its most favourable end: if the family cannot pass on these books under the haircut, it cannot pass anywhere, and no wider universe may be shopped ex post. Extending the universe requires a new declaration.

evaluation_bar.costs: TWO cost stacks, both must pass every component. Programme stack: programme fees/slippage (simulator.Costs = 5 bps fee + 3 bps slippage per fill = 16 bps round trip) PLUS the declared adverse-selection allowance of 5 bps per fill — 13 bps per fill, 26 bps effective round trip. 2x shadow stack: doubled fees/slippage (Costs(10, 6) = 32 bps round trip) PLUS the same 5 bps per fill allowance — 21 bps per fill, 42 bps effective round trip. The allowance is a haircut, not a fee, so the shadow doubles only the fee/slippage component.
evaluation_bar.holdout: rd.common.holdout_check must pass (per-symbol: >= 2 of 3 symbols with positive expectancy on >= 20 OOS trades each, and no single symbol contributing more than 80% of total net profit)
evaluation_bar.judgement: OOS only, walk-forward folds W1..W5 with entry-time attribution; parameters are frozen by this declaration — nothing is selected in-sample
evaluation_bar.multiple_testing: Bonferroni one-sided t-test on pooled OOS per-trade net returns, p < 0.05/N, against the programme trial floor at run time (programme counter = 3,891 declared trials as of 2026-11-17 per the discovery census; SRS's declared cell takes it to 3,892 when run and S-RD1's to 3,893; this declaration adds exactly ONE further trial — a single frozen cell — and the run must state the floor it used, read from the rd-reconcile ledger; the runner has no default)
evaluation_bar.source: Stratex/rigorous_backtest/rd/common.py PROMOTION_BAR + programme practice; strict OOS PF < 1.2 closes and deletes the family per the owner's standing rule

fill_model.adverse_selection_rationale: A passive fill is information: a resting order is filled disproportionately when aggressive flow is pushing through its level and the short-horizon move continues against the maker. Published markout estimates for passive BTC fills at minute horizons sit in the low single digits to ~10 bps. 5 bps per fill — exactly the programme's own taker fee, so it cannot be dismissed as a token allowance — is charged on EVERY fill (buys, grid sells, teardown and end-of-data exits alike; one rule, no exceptions) at both cost stacks.
fill_model.fee_model: Programme standard (rigorous_backtest.simulator.Costs) applied PER FILL: 5 bps taker fee + 3 bps spread/slippage per fill (16 bps round trip); the 2x shadow doubles both (10 + 6 per fill, 32 bps round trip). Costs are applied adversely in price space, identical in form to simulator._net_return for a long trade.
fill_model.fill_price: The level price exactly (limit-order semantics: a real limit order fills at its limit or better once its level trades through).
fill_model.trade_through_rationale: Top-of-book spreads for BTCUSDT / ETHUSDT / SOLUSDT on Binance are ~1-3 bps. A resting order at a merely TOUCHED level fills only if the entire queue ahead of it happens to clear, which a touch does not imply — naive grid simulators that fill on touch manufacture most of their apparent edge here. Requiring the bar's extreme to exceed the level by 10 bps (roughly 3-10x the spread, and a substantial fraction of a typical 15m bar's range) means aggressive flow demonstrably consumed the level and printed beyond it. The rule additionally requires the bar's range to SPAN the level (for a buy, the bar must have traded at or above P): a level the bar never reached cannot have been crossed within it, and filling there would manufacture trades at unvisited prices. Gap-through bars (whose range lies entirely beyond the level) therefore do NOT fill — a deliberately conservative miss, since a real resting order would fill at the gap open; missed fills bias against the family, phantom fills would bias for it. This is the family's central honesty mechanism; it is frozen, and loosening it would be a new declaration.
fill_model.trade_through_rule: A resting BUY at level P fills in bar i ONLY if bar i's range SPANS the level and trades THROUGH it downward: bar i's high >= P AND bar i's low <= P x (1 - 0.001) — price must reach the level and trade through it by 10 bps, not merely touch it. A resting SELL at level P fills ONLY if bar i's low <= P AND bar i's high >= P x (1 + 0.001). A bar whose range does not reach the level cannot fill it, and a touch without the through-margin is NO fill; such touches are counted in the run's stats (touch_no_fill) as the rejected fantasy fills.

hypothesis: On 15-minute bars, a causally-placed long-only grid (trailing 7-day P10-P90 range, 10 arithmetic intervals, re-placed every 24h, one unit per line, paired one-step exits) harvests enough range oscillation on the three most liquid Binance USDT-M pairs to clear the RD programme bar EVEN AFTER a pre-declared fill haircut that removes the two known simulator fantasies — touch fills (excluded by a 10 bps trade-through requirement) and free fills (every fill pays programme fees plus a 5 bps adverse-selection allowance). The census tension is the test: with too little haircut the run measures the simulator, with too much nothing survives; this declaration freezes the haircut first and lets the bar decide.
promotion_path: Passing the bar makes this a forward-test CANDIDATE only, under the Phase-3 forward protocol (>= 100 trades AND >= 8 weeks on demo), with the forward sizing mapping declared in declared_conventions.forward_sizing. Nothing here authorises live trading.

rules.frequency: Grids are placed continuously over the whole loaded series (in-sample and out-of-sample alike; only OOS-entered trades are judged). One unit per line per symbol; a line may re-buy on a later bar once its previous unit has exited (subject to the same-bar rule in declared_conventions.fill_sequencing).
rules.grid_construction: At a placement bar's close: lower = 10th percentile and upper = 90th percentile of the trailing 672 bar closes (type-7 linear-interpolation percentiles over completed bars only); 11 lines L_k = lower + k x (upper - lower) / 10 for k = 0..10 (arithmetic spacing, step = (upper - lower) / 10). Lines are frozen for the whole epoch — no intra-epoch adaptation, no re-centring.
rules.inventory_cap: At most ONE open unit per buy line and at most 10 open units per symbol at any time (structural: there are exactly 10 buy lines). A buy signal on a line whose unit is already open does not exist — the line is simply occupied.
rules.no_lookahead: Placement uses only bars completed at the placement bar's close (the trailing window ends AT that bar). Fills are evaluated bar by bar after placement. Percentiles, ranges and lines never see a future bar.
rules.parameters_fixed: TIMEFRAME=15m, SYMBOLS=[BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT], TRAILING_WINDOW_BARS=672, RANGE_LOW_PCT=10, RANGE_HIGH_PCT=90, GRID_INTERVALS=10, EPOCH_BARS=96, TRADE_THROUGH_MARGIN=0.001 (10 bps), ADVERSE_SELECTION_BPS_PER_FILL=5.0 — no other variants are authorised under this declaration; trying variants means new declarations and a higher trial count. This declaration is exactly ONE trial.
rules.placement_cadence: First placement at the close of bar index 671 (the first bar with a full 672-bar trailing window), then every 96 bars (24h) at that bar's close. The grid placed at bar j is active for bars j+1 .. j+96; at bar j+96's close the epoch ends (teardown, then the next placement).
rules.range_definition: Trailing window ONLY: the 672 completed 15m bars (7 days) ending at the placement bar. Percentiles are taken over the window's CLOSES. The range is never a future range, never a full-sample range, and never hand-set.
rules.teardown: At every placement bar's close, all open units are force-closed at that close (exit_reason TEARDOWN) with full per-fill costs, before the new grid is placed. Units still open after the final bar are closed at the final close (exit_reason END_OF_DATA) on the same terms.
rules.unit_entry: Line L_k (k = 0..9) opens one long unit when a bar spans it and trades through it downward (bar high >= L_k and bar low <= L_k x (1 - 0.001)); entry price = L_k; entry time = that bar. Line L_10 never buys (it has no line above it inside the grid).
rules.unit_exit: A unit opened on line L_k exits when a later bar spans L_(k+1) and trades through it upward (bar low <= L_(k+1) and bar high >= L_(k+1) x (1 + 0.001)); exit price = L_(k+1); exit_reason GRID_SELL. Otherwise it exits only by teardown or end-of-data. There is no stop-loss and no take-profit beyond the paired line — that absence is the strategy, and its risk is carried by the inventory cap and the 24h teardown.

source: FRIDAY Universe strategy-discovery census, 2026-11-17 (~/workspace/str-discovery-census/CENSUS.md), recommended slate #7: 'Grid / passive MM, crypto 15m, with pre-declared fill haircut'. Census section 3b: the repo module Stratex/strategies/grid_trading.py is NOT_EVALUABLE (no callable get_signal through the standard path) and is one of only two never-evaluated repo modules that are not re-skins; the grid / passive-market-making mechanism has never been declared or judged by any RD round. Census section 3c caveat, adopted as this declaration's core: 'kline-simulated grid fills are systematically optimistic (no queue position, no adverse selection). A bar run needs a declared fill haircut or it proves nothing.' DISPOSITION OF THE REPO MODULE (read in full from origin/main at declaration time): the harness REPLACES grid_trading.py rather than reusing it — (1) it has no callable signal path, which is why it was never evaluable; (2) its fill rule is a touch fill on a single price print with zero fees anywhere — exactly the fantasy-fill mechanism the haircut exists to eliminate; (3) its levels alternate buy/sell by index parity rather than resting buys below / sells above an anchor with paired exits, so it is not a functional grid book; (4) its adapt_grid re-centres bounds on the current price with no causal placement rule; (5) it has no inventory limits or exposure accounting. The module is left untouched in the repo. Adjacent evidence, disclosed before the run: directional and reversion families on this panel class have overwhelmingly failed the bar (RD-001..RD-016; pairs died gross-of-costs in RD-006); no grid or liquidity-provision family has ever been judged, so there is no direct prior — the honest prior for a new OHLCV-derived family in this programme is negative, and the fill-haircut design exists because grid backtests in particular are known to flatter themselves.
